text:
dinesh: Heads-up — after the FA v3 canary rollout yesterday we're seeing a consistent p95 spike on small-batch, mid-sequence workloads. Baseline (v2) p95 ~42ms, v3 canary p95 ~58ms. Same model, same batcher config. Anyone else seeing this?

carla: saw the alert. quick traces show extra workspace allocations and a handful of allocator retries. GPU memcopy activity is higher too.

emily: can we get kernel_choice telemetry? don't have enough signal to know whether v3 is choosing a different kernel path for short sequences.

jarod: ran a quick perf sweep this morning (1000 inferences, seq_len mix [8,16,64]):
- v2 throughput ~1200 tps, p95 44ms
- v3 throughput ~980 tps, p95 58ms
- p50 roughly equal
So it's tail-oriented, seems workload-shape dependent.

carla: hypothesis: crossover between the "small-workspace" fused kernel in v2 and the new dispatch rules in v3 triggers extra allocations + memcpy for certain seq/batch combos. fragmentation increases over time and spikes p95.

emily: agree. we should add these telemetry keys ASAP: kernel_choice, workspace_alloc_bytes, alloc_retry_count, alloc_frag_ratio, seq_len, batch_size. Also a per-request flag for pinned_kernel to help reproduce.

jarod: allocator dump from one failing run (abbreviated):
```
workspace_pool_size=128MB
active_allocs=23
largest_free_chunk=8MB
alloc_retry_count=7
peak_workspace_used=93MB
alloc_frag_ratio=0.34
```
That frag ratio looks non-trivial for our short-seq heavy traces.

dinesh: nice. another quick note: some traces show kernel_choice=flashv3_bf16_matmul which differs from v2's fp16 fused path — maybe precision path changes influence workspace layout.

carla: +1 on the precision angle. v3 introduced BF16-optimized matmul for some shapes; memory layout differs and can increase temporary buffer requirements.

emily: proposed immediate steps: 1) enable kernel_choice + alloc telemetry in canary (low overhead counters). 2) run workspace_pool sweep (64MB/128MB/256MB) for shape permutations. 3) add shortseq sampling to nightly perf suite. 4) allow model-manifest pinning of kernel for shortseq-heavy customers.

jarod: I'll add a perf-run job. command to run locally: `./perf-runner --model rwinf/gpt-small --shapes "8x1,16x2,64x4" --kernel-candidates fa_v2,fa_v3 --workspace-pool 128`

carla: one more idea: implement a quick allocator patch to reserve a small-slab for tiny workspaces to reduce fragmentation. low-risk toggle behind flag.

dinesh: action items assigned: dinesh -> collate canary traces + define p95 rollout gate (suggested gate: p95_shortseq < 45ms and alloc_frag_ratio < 0.15). carla -> allocator small-slab patch + open PR. jarod -> perf-run jobs + run pool sweep. emily -> telemetry flag + shape heatmap.

infra-bot: deployed feature flag `kernel_choice_telemetry=true` to canary group at 1799995000.

jarod: quick interim experiment results after pool sweep (canary, 10k inferences):
- pool=64MB -> p95 63ms, alloc_frag_ratio 0.41
- pool=128MB -> p95 52ms, alloc_frag_ratio 0.27
- pool=256MB -> p95 46ms, alloc_frag_ratio 0.12
So larger pool helps but memory cost rises.

emily: good signal. we need to weigh memory cost vs tail latency. maybe auto-sizing policy: increase pool only for models with high shortseq_percent.

carla: opened PR with small-slab allocator toggle: reduces shortseq p95 by ~6ms in local sims. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7821 :thumbsup:

dinesh: solid. let's keep v3 canary but add a shortseq pin to v2 for affected customers until we tune. i'll draft a short RFC addendum with rollout gating and telemetry schema. thanks all.

emily: FYI I'll add kernel_choice & alloc metrics to the console dashboards so PMs can see impact by customer.

dinesh: closing loop — we'll reconvene after the next 12h canary run. obrigado :raised_hands:
